evals.name: nearby-search-index
evals.prompt: Design the search for 'restaurants within 500 m' over 200M businesses with 5,000 QPS. Which spatial index and why?
evals.expected_output: Geohash of length 6 for 500 m, query the cell plus its 8 neighbours, business IDs per geohash cached in Redis, ranked by distance; quadtree and S2 compared; business table sharded by ID, geohash table replicated not sharded, citing Vol. 2 ch. 1.
expectations: Chooses a geohash precision matching the radius (length 6 for about 500 m).
Includes the 8 neighbouring cells to handle boundary cases.
Caches geohash → business IDs and business_id → details in Redis, explaining why coordinates are a bad cache key.
Compares geohash with quadtree (and optionally S2) on density adaptivity and update cost.
Cites Vol. 2 ch. 1 (or chapter 16 in the upstream numbering).

evals.name: live-location-fanout
evals.prompt: 10M concurrent users share their location every 30 seconds with ~400 friends each. How do updates reach friends' phones and how many Redis nodes do we need?
evals.expected_output: WebSocket servers per client, Redis pub/sub with one channel per user, ~334k updates/s fanning out to ~40 online friends each (~14M pushes/s), roughly 140 Redis servers by CPU not memory, hash ring in ZooKeeper, TTL location cache, citing Vol. 2 ch. 2.
expectations: Computes about 334k location updates per second.
Uses a per-user pub/sub channel with WebSocket servers subscribing for their connected users' friends.
Sizes the Redis cluster by push throughput (about 140 servers), not by memory.
Mentions consistent hashing / service discovery for channel placement and the resubscription cost of resizing.
Cites Vol. 2 ch. 2 (or chapter 17 in the upstream numbering).
